/-!
# Erdős Problem 1038

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
 - [Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025
  (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
-/

open scoped Real ENNReal
open MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos1038

/-- What is the infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such
that all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.parts.i (n : ℕ) : answer(sorry) =
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

/-- The supremum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2)`. This is proved in
[Tao25]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.parts.ii (n : ℕ) : 2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) =
    ⨆ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

/-- The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `< 1.835`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.variants.inf_upperBound (n : ℕ) : ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} < 1.835 := by
  sorry

/-- The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `≥ 2 ^ (4 / 3) - 1`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.varaints.inf_lowerBound (n : ℕ) : 2 ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ) - 1 ≤
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

end Erdos1038

reformulations.difference: Nonconstancy is expressed as `f ≠ 1` under monicity, and real-rootedness with all roots in [-1,1] is expressed by the cardinality of a filtered root multiset equalling `f.natDegree`. The same root encoding is used throughout the file.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every real polynomial, the filtered-root cardinality is at most `f.roots.card`, which is at most `f.natDegree`. Equality therefore forces the filter to retain every root and forces the total root cardinality to equal the degree. Mathlib's `splits_iff_card_roots` then gives splitting over ℝ, so no nonreal roots are omitted. Conversely, splitting with all roots in the interval gives the stated cardinality equality. Multiplicities are retained. For a monic polynomial, `f ≠ 1` is equivalent to positive natural degree. These predicate equivalences were proved in `/workspace/review/equivalences.lean`.

reformulations.difference: The supremum includes constant monic polynomials, whereas the source restricts to nonconstant polynomials.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only constant monic real polynomial is 1. Its strict sublevel set `{x | |1| < 1}` is empty and has measure 0, so adding it cannot change a supremum of nonnegative measures. The nonconstant family is nonempty, with X giving measure 2. Equality of the two suprema and the resulting equivalence of the supremum statements were proved in `/workspace/review/equivalences.lean`.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The strict upper bound is supported explicitly by Sothanaphan's post 2351 (a construction with length between 1.8344 and 1.8345) and Tao's post 2352, which states `2^(4/3) - 1 ≤ inf < 1.835` and `sup = 2√2`. Thus the site's abbreviated `1.835…` is not a rounding defect in the Lean statement. The unused natural-number parameters are harmless: the source takes extrema over all degrees, and universal quantification over an unused ℕ parameter is equivalent to the unparameterized claim. The answer slot has the intended type ℝ≥0∞ and is constrained by equality to the infimum. Independent Lean checks in `equivalences.lean` and `boundary.lean` compile without errors or warnings; they cover zero and constant polynomials, repeated roots, endpoint roots, rejection of nonreal and out-of-range roots, exact arithmetic constants, measurability, and finite bounds on the extrema. These checks do not rely on the problem's sorry proofs. The source still records the infimum problem as open; its separate unvetted full-proof claims do not establish a status discrepancy.
